clue.text: A few alerts about tiny crustaceans

indicators.note: 'about' can mean round and round or every which way, so the letters are moved around into a new order

blocks.note: taken letter for letter as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone is issuing a handful of warnings about minuscule shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A few alerts' reads like a phrase about warnings, but its ten letters are exactly the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Water fleas such as Daphnia are minute freshwater crustaceans, so the phrase is a description of that group.

clue.text: Winery’s first fruit crop

indicators.note: 'first' asks for only the opening letter of the word it attaches to

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a hip is the fruit of the rose

explanation.surface: A vineyard's first harvest of grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit crop' looks like one phrase about harvests; 'crop' is split off as the definition, the short whip carried by a rider.
explanation.definitionFit: A riding crop is a short horse whip, so the two words are synonyms in the equestrian sense.

clue.text: Danced like a pervert

blocks.note: first meaning: did the Twist, the 1960s dance craze
second meaning: warped or perverted in mind

explanation.surface: Someone moved on the dance floor in a creepy manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The Twist was a popular 1960s dance, so the past tense of dancing it is the same word as the adjective for a warped mind.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves both as the past tense of doing that dance and as an adjective for someone sick or perverse.

clue.text: Church member a monarchic lot abused

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters are put into a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is mistreated by a gang of royalists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monarchic lot' sounds like a political faction, but the three words supply exactly thirteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman Catholic belongs to the Church headed by the Pope, so the person is a member of that denomination.

clue.text: Desert boy raised to make bread

blocks.note: to desert someone is to leave them
Ned is a boy's name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A lad brought up in the desert grows up to become a baker.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' looks like a reversal signal for the boy, but the boy reads downwards as written; 'raised' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Dough that has been leavened is made to rise with yeast or another agent, as most bread is.

clue.text: Paul’s second long letter

indicators.note: 'second' points to the letter in position two of the word it attaches to

blocks.note: the name spelt P-A-U-L, taking its second letter
to long for something is to itch for it

explanation.surface: St Paul's second lengthy epistle to one of the churches.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Paul's epistles in the Bible, but the clue wants a single letter of the alphabet spelt out as a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the written name of the eighth character of the alphabet, H, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Animal run over

indicators.note: turned over, a word lies the other way up, so its letters read backwards

blocks.note: water runs, or flows

explanation.surface: A creature has been hit by a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run over' looks like a phrasal verb for roadkill; it splits into the word to turn and the turning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild carnivorous mammal of the dog family, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Old rover’s bar runs drugs

indicators.note: to bar something is to exclude it, so the named letter is kept out

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a rover is an old word for a sea robber; the 's is read as a plural
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An old wanderer's pub deals in narcotics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a pub, but it means excluding; a rover in the old sense is a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are narcotics derived from opium, such as morphine and heroin, so they are a class of drugs.

clue.text: Fine day enveloping ladies with soft illumination

indicators.note: to envelop is to wrap round, so the outer pieces surround another

blocks.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
the ladies is a women's toilet, a loo
D is the abbreviation for day
a soft touch is a light touch

explanation.surface: On a fine day, women are bathed in gentle light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft illumination' looks like one phrase, but 'soft' gives letters and only 'illumination' defines; 'the ladies' is British for a women's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A floodlight is a broad, intense beam lamp used to light stadiums and buildings, a form of artificial illumination.

clue.text: Part of a hip Paris destination

blocks.note: first meaning: the broad upper bone of the pelvis
second meaning: the Latin name of Troy, where the Trojan prince Paris took Helen

explanation.surface: Somewhere fashionable to visit in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris' looks like the French city, but it is the Trojan prince who carried Helen home to Troy; 'hip' looks like trendy but is anatomical.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the uppermost pelvic bone and, in Latin, the city of Troy in Homer's legend.

clue.text: Very high voice holding one girl back

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside, so one piece sits within another
going back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the letters read right to left

blocks.note: the alto is a singing voice
I is the Roman numeral for one
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A soprano's top register is keeping a young woman from going forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very high voice' looks like the definition, but 'voice' gives the outer letters; the reversed girl goes in after the one.
explanation.definitionFit: Altissimo is the musical term for the very highest register of an instrument or voice, Italian for 'highest'.

clue.text: Pal senses she’s suffering lack of form

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, damaged, so the letters are put out of their order

blocks.note: the fodder, thirteen letters with the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A friend can tell that she is not in good shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack of form' sounds like an athlete off form, but here it means having no definite shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no definite outline or structure is being amorphous, so the abstract noun names that absence.

clue.text: Kind of advance notice about painting

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so one word goes round another

blocks.note: to tender money is to offer or advance it
to take notice is to heed
painting is an art

explanation.surface: Some sort of early warning concerning a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind of' reads as 'a sort of', but 'Kind' is the adjective meaning gentle and compassionate.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender-hearted person is compassionate and easily moved, which is what a kind person is.

clue.text: Star chess player, one of seven

blocks.note: one of the two sides in chess is White
one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: A celebrated chess grandmaster belongs to a team of seven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star chess player' reads as a top player, but 'Star' is the definition; the seven are Snow White's companions.
explanation.definitionFit: A white dwarf is the small dense remnant of a burnt-out star, so astronomers class it as a type of star.

clue.text: Adds water to so called cover charges

indicators.note: 'so called' means named this way, as if spoken, so the words count by their sound

blocks.note: to cover is to hide, and charges are rates

explanation.surface: A restaurant waters down its so-called service charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover charges' looks like a restaurant fee, but it is two separate words, a verb for concealing and a noun for prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To hydrate something is to supply it with moisture or combine it with water, the chemical and everyday sense alike.

clue.text: At Le Mans I finally look into its sporty vehicle

indicators.note: 'finally' asks for only the closing letter of the word that follows it
something sporty is lively and frisky, so these letters jump about into a new order
going into something puts one piece inside another

blocks.note: Le Mans is in France, where the word for I is je
taken as written, as fodder
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: At the famous French motor race, someone at last gets a look at a racing car.
explanation.walkthrough: Le Mans suggests motor racing, so 'sporty vehicle' looks like one phrase for a racing car; 'sporty' is the anagram signal and only 'vehicle' defines. Placing a French town before a word asks for it in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet ski is a small motorised watercraft ridden like a motorbike on water, so it is a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Swimmer from Bow’s more attractive after drink

indicators.note: Bow is in Cockney east London, where speakers drop the H at the front of words

blocks.note: the drink is slang for the sea
hot means attractive, so more attractive is hotter

explanation.surface: A Cockney swimmer looks better looking after a few drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of the East End of London, home of the Cockney accent that drops initial H; 'the drink' is slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea otters are marine mammals of the Pacific that spend almost all their lives in the water, so they are swimmers.

clue.text: Ancient city pub’s entered for award

indicators.note: something that has entered is now inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Troy is the ancient city of the Iliad
PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

explanation.surface: A historic town's pub has been put forward for a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: PH is the abbreviation on British maps for a public house; the pub goes inside the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A trophy is a cup or other prize given to a winner, so it is an award.

clue.text: Doctor filling in locum roster

indicators.note: the filling of something is what lies inside it, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: the word without its outer letters
a roster is a list of names

explanation.surface: A medic is covering a shift on the stand-in rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling in' suggests a locum filling in for a colleague, but it means the inside letters of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An oculist is an old name for an eye specialist, a physician who treats sight problems.

clue.text: Restless, always cutting school

indicators.note: a blade cutting something goes into it, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: a school is a group of fish, so school stands for fish
ever means always

explanation.surface: A fidgety pupil keeps skipping lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting school' looks like truancy, but a school here is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish can describe agitated, frantic activity or nervous excitement, a state of being unable to settle.

clue.text: Establish how VIPs when late sometimes lie

definitions.text: how VIPs when late sometimes lie

blocks.note: first meaning: to install someone in office

blocks.clueFragment: how VIPs when late sometimes lie
blocks.note: second meaning: read as two words, how a dead dignitary's body is displayed before burial

explanation.surface: Finding out the excuses that important people give for turning up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means dead, not tardy, and 'lie' means rest, not fib: an eminent person's coffin may lie in state.
explanation.definitionFit: To instate is to place someone formally in a position, so it means establishing them there.

clue.text: Latin scores were made up by these cheats

definitions.text: Latin scores were made up by these

blocks.clueFragment: Latin scores were made up by these
blocks.note: first meaning: a score is twenty, written XX in Roman numerals, a pair of crosses
second meaning: betrays someone by a deceitful trick

explanation.surface: Fiddled exam marks in Latin were the work of fraudsters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin scores' suggests marks in a Latin exam; it is the Roman way of writing twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to betray a partner after pretending to co-operate, so it is a synonym for deceiving.

clue.text: What sailors did sounded vulgar

indicators.note: something sounded is spoken out, so it counts by how it is said rather than spelt

blocks.note: sailors man a ship, so they crewed it

explanation.surface: Sailors' talk came across as coarse.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the cliché of sailors swearing; 'did' means what they did to a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude and vulgar are synonyms for coarse or offensive in taste and language.

clue.text: Let rip!

blocks.note: first meaning: leased out for payment
second meaning: a tear in fabric

explanation.walkthrough: 'Let rip' looks like an exhortation to cut loose; it is two separate words, each meaning the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for leasing property and as a noun for a split or tear in cloth.

clue.text: Battle spirit adopted by a tribunal

indicators.note: something adopted is taken into a family, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
gin is a spirit
a tribunal is a court

explanation.surface: A fighting spirit is taken up by a panel of judges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battle spirit' reads as fighting spirit, but 'Battle' is the definition; the gin sits between the article and the court.
explanation.definitionFit: Agincourt is the 1415 battle in which Henry V's English army defeated the French, so it names a battle.

clue.text: Clear time to sunbathe on vacation

indicators.note: a vacated building is emptied, so the word loses everything but its outer letters

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
only the first and last letters survive

explanation.surface: A free stretch of time for lying in the sun while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' reads as on holiday, which fits sunbathing; here it means emptied out.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a board or a record is to wipe it, so the verbs are synonyms in the sense of removing content.

clue.text: Newspaper article covering English cheese

indicators.note: a cover goes over and round something, so the outer pieces wrap another

blocks.note: the FT, the Financial Times
the indefinite article
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A press piece reporting on a British cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newspaper article' reads as a single story, but the paper and the article are separate pieces; the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Feta is a white brined Greek curd made from sheep's or goat's milk, an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Commie mostly held in regard, looking back

definitions.note: a noun phrase: the act of looking back

indicators.note: 'mostly' means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
held inside something, one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: to hold someone in regard is to respect them
Trot is slang for a Trotskyist, a hard-left communist

explanation.surface: A communist, held in high esteem, is reflecting on the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held in regard' reads as esteemed, but 'held in' is the instruction and 'regard' is the outer word.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrospect is a survey or review of past events, the act of looking back, as in the phrase 'in retrospect'.
